who: Stephen R. MacKinnon, historian of modern China at Arizona State University; PhD UC Davis, 1971.

evidence.says: ASU identifies Stephen MacKinnon as a history professor, trained at UC Davis, who taught modern Chinese history and graduate seminars.
The 2008–2009 faculty list records Stephen R. Mackinnon, History professor, PhD University of California Davis, 1971.
Authority for Stephen R. MacKinnon identifies the author of Power and Politics in Late Imperial China and an Arizona State history professor.

notes: Exact doctoral institution and year agree; institution and Chinese-history specialization fit the listed students.

who: Jehangir Yezdi Malegam, medieval historian at Duke University; PhD Stanford, 2006.

evidence.says: Duke lists Jehangir Malegam as Associate Professor of History with a Stanford PhD awarded in 2006.
Meghan Woolley’s 2022 Duke history dissertation, The Heart of the Court, names Jehangir Malegam as supervisor.
Authority for Jehangir Yezdi Malegam identifies the author of The Sleep of Behemoth as a Duke history professor.

notes: Exact doctorate and direct supervision of a listed student establish the match; the authority supplies the fuller name.

who: Marlene J. Mayo, historian of modern Japan at the University of Maryland; PhD Columbia, 1961.

evidence.says: Maryland identifies Marlene J. Mayo as Associate Professor Emerita of History, specializing in Japan, with a Columbia doctorate in East Asian history.
The 1996–1997 Maryland catalogue lists Marlene J. Mayo as Associate Professor of History and records Columbia graduate study and a 1961 PhD.
The candidate item identifies Marlene J. Mayo as a historian employed at Maryland and links LC authority no00025717.

notes: University, field and doctoral institution/year agree with the supervisor record and the students’ Japan-related research.

who: Richard Patrick McCormick, historian of American politics and New Jersey at Rutgers; PhD Pennsylvania, 1948.

evidence.says: Rutgers archives identify Richard Patrick McCormick, teaching in its history department from 1945, and record his Pennsylvania doctorate in 1948 for Experiment in Independence.
Authority identifies Richard Patrick McCormick as the author of Experiment in Independence and The Presidential Game.
Rutgers identifies Richard L. McCormick separately and records his history PhD at Yale in 1976.

notes: The exact Pennsylvania 1948 doctorate selects Richard Patrick; the alternative Richard L. has a different doctorate. This verdict does not independently verify every listed student attribution.

who: Robert C. McMath Jr., historian of American populism at Georgia Tech and Arkansas; PhD UNC Chapel Hill, 1972.

evidence.says: Arkansas reports that Robert C. McMath joined it in 2005 after 33 years teaching history and holding administrative posts at Georgia Tech; his doctorate was UNC Chapel Hill, 1972.
Arkansas specifies that McMath’s 1972 UNC Chapel Hill doctorate was in American history.
Authority identifies Robert C. (Robert Carroll) McMath Jr., author of Populist Vanguard, as a Georgia Institute of Technology professor of social sciences.

notes: Exact doctorate matches; his Georgia Tech and Arkansas appointments cover the listed supervision institutions and years.

who: Elizabeth A. Meyer, historian of Greek and Roman law and society at the University of Virginia; PhD Yale, 1988.

evidence.says: Virginia identifies Elizabeth A. Meyer as a history professor specializing in Greek and Roman history and records her Yale PhD, 1988.
Her CV records continuous Virginia history appointments from 1988 and a Yale history PhD in December 1988 on literacy and law in the Roman Empire.
Authority for Elizabeth A. Meyer identifies the author of Legitimacy and Law in the Roman World as affiliated with the University of Virginia.

notes: Exact doctorate, institutional chronology and ancient legal-history field agree.

who: David O. Morgan, historian of medieval Iran and the Mongol Empire at Wisconsin–Madison; PhD London, 1977.

evidence.says: Wisconsin identifies David O. Morgan, specialist in Islamic and Middle Eastern history, as joining its faculty in 1999 and retiring in 2010; his PhD was London, 1977.
Molly Patterson’s memorial identifies David Orrin Morgan as her academic advisor at Wisconsin–Madison and records his London doctorate in 1977.
The candidate item identifies David O. Morgan, employed at Wisconsin–Madison, educated at London, with LC authority n86036311.

notes: Direct testimony from listed student Molly Patterson establishes the Wisconsin match. The supplied UNC Chapel Hill 1968 own_phd conflicts with his documented London 1977 doctorate and should not be carried over to this candidate.

who: José C. Moya, historian of Latin America and migration at UCLA and Barnard; PhD Rutgers, 1988.

evidence.says: UCLA identifies Jose Moya as Professor Emeritus, arriving after his Rutgers PhD in 1988, teaching Latin American history and directing doctoral dissertations.
Barnard identifies José C. Moya as a history professor, author of Cousins and Strangers, with a Rutgers PhD.
Authority for Jose C. Moya identifies the author of Cousins and Strangers, formerly teaching at UCLA for 17 years and joining Barnard in 2005.

notes: Exact doctorate and UCLA history appointment match; the authority connects the fuller candidate name to the same historian.
